Replace matches

Source: R/replace.R
re_replace.Rd

re_replace() replaces matches in each element of x, all of them by default. re_expand() returns a template expanded with each element's first match, as Python's Match.expand() does.

Usage

re_replace(
  x,
  pattern,
  replacement,
  n = Inf,
  syntax = c("extended", "literal"),
  limits = NULL
)

re_expand(x, pattern, template, limits = NULL)

Arguments

x

A character vector, a raw vector, or a list of raw vectors. NA (or NULL in a list) gives NA.

pattern

A character vector or an re vector; see Patterns.

replacement

A character vector of templates, of length 1 or the length of x, or a function; see Templates and Replacement functions. An NA template gives NA.

n

The most matches to replace per element, Inf for all.

syntax

"extended" or "literal"; see Templates.

limits

A re_limits() object, or NULL for getOption("zuregex.limits") and then PCRE2's defaults.

template

A character vector of templates, of length 1 or the length of x.

Value

A character vector as long as x. Elements without a match are returned unchanged by re_replace() and as NA by re_expand(). Other strings are in UTF-8, or marked as "bytes" for bytes input.

Templates

With syntax = "extended", the default, templates use PCRE2's extended substitution syntax, not base R's \\1:

TemplateMeaning
$1, ${12}, ${name}A group by number, past nine, or by name. $0 is the whole match.
${1:-none}The group, or none when it did not take part in the match.
${1:+yes:no}yes when the group took part, otherwise no.
\U...\E, \L...\E, \u, \lUpper or lower case until \E, or for one character.
$$, \$A literal $.

A group that did not take part in the match is replaced by "". A reference to a group that does not exist, or a malformed template, raises zuregex_error_template when a match first uses it. With syntax = "literal" the replacement is inserted as it is.

Replacement functions

replacement may be a function. It is called once for the whole call, if anything matched, with a data frame of every match: element, match (its number within the element), 0 (the matched text) and one column per group, named as in re_match(). It must return a character vector with one replacement per row.

Patterns

pattern is a character vector of regular expressions, compiled through the cache with the default options, or an re vector from re_compile() for flags, dialects and literal patterns. It has length 1, used for every element of x, or exactly the length of x, pairing pattern[i] with x[i]. Any other length is an error: nothing is recycled. An NA pattern gives NA for its element.

Strings and bytes

Character input is matched as UTF-8; strings in other declared encodings are translated first. Invalid UTF-8 is an error of class zuregex_error_utf. A raw vector is one subject matched as bytes, as is each element of a list of raw vectors, and so is a character vector with any element marked as "bytes". Patterns are then compiled without UTF-8 support, so . matches one byte.

Examples

x <- c("2026-10-21", "no date", NA)
re_replace(x, "(\\d{4})-(\\d{2})-(\\d{2})", "$3/$2/$1")
#> [1] "21/10/2026" "no date"    NA          
re_replace(x, "(?<y>\\d{4})", "${y}!")
#> [1] "2026!-10-21" "no date"     NA           
re_replace("hello world", "(\\w+)", "\\u$1")
#> [1] "Hello World"
re_replace("a1b22", "\\d+", function(m) strrep("#", nchar(m[["0"]])))
#> [1] "a#b##"
re_expand("John Smith", "(\\w+) (\\w+)", "$2, $1")
#> [1] "Smith, John"
